He attempted to speak, but his words were noticeably slurred, making them difficult to fully comprehend. He pointed to his right arm and then his right leg, indicating weakness.

"So, you're feeling weakness on your right side?" I clarified. He nodded slowly. "And when did this start?"

He struggled to articulate a precise time, looking to his wife for assistance. His wife reiterated, "He was fine at breakfast, around 7 AM. Then around 8:30 AM, he started having trouble holding his coffee cup and his words became muddled."

"Okay, so roughly 90 minutes ago, potentially a bit longer," I noted. "Any headache? Numbness or tingling?"

He shook his head, indicating no headache or numbness. His wife confirmed, "Just the weakness and the speech."

Vitals were taken: BP 180/100 mmHg, HR 78 bpm, RR 16 bpm, SpO2 98% on room air. On neurological exam, I noted right facial droop, right upper extremity drift, and decreased strength in the right upper and lower extremities. Speech was dysarthric.

"No, this is new for me."

"Any significant medical history I should be aware of? Surgeries, chronic conditions?"

"Alright, let's take a look. I'll just palpate your abdomen. Please let me know if anything is tender."

[During palpation] "Right here, Sneha, take a deep breath in."
